# /lettering

## Purpose

Put the words on the page where they can be read in the right order
without covering what the panel is about. The text itself is already in
`page.yaml`. This command plans where each balloon, caption, and sound
effect sits, delivers it in the project's lettering mode, and checks the
result against the script character by character. In `in_image` mode the
image model draws the lettering. In `overlay` mode the art is generated
without text and the lettering is set on top from `lettering.yaml`.

## Use When

- Pages are scripted and their lettering needs a placement plan before
  generation.
- Overlay mode: a page has a reviewed render and needs its lettered output.
- A review failed the `lettering` check: a wrong word, a missing accent, a
  tail that points at the wrong speaker, a balloon over a face.
- The project switches lettering mode.

## Inputs

- `issue` (ID, required): the `ISS_###` to letter.
- `pages` (ID or range, optional): limit the run; default is every page of
  the issue.
- `render` (ID, optional, default the page's `current_render`): the render
  an overlay sits on.
- `mode` (enum, optional, default `lettering.mode` in `project.yaml`):
  `in_image` | `overlay`.
- `--check` (flag, optional): check existing lettering against `page.yaml`
  and report; change nothing.

## Invokes Agents

- letterer
- visual-reviewer

## Required Skills

- balloon-lettering

## Process

1. Read `lettering` (`mode`, `font_family`, `case`, word limits),
   `language`, and `reading_direction` from `project.yaml`, and the
   lettering section of the style bible.
2. Audit the text in each page file. Every element has the exact words and
   accents in the project's language, a `type`, a `speaker` for spoken
   types who is in the panel's `cast`, and an `order` that is unique in the
   page and follows the reading order. Word counts are inside
   `max_words_per_balloon` and `max_words_per_panel`. Send a line that is
   too long back to `/panel-script`; do not trim it here.
3. Plan the placement of each element: which area of the panel it takes,
   so that it covers no face, no hand, and no part of the action; where the
   tail starts and that it ends at the speaker's mouth; and that the first
   balloon to be read sits where the eye enters the panel for the
   project's reading direction. Sound effects sit beside their source.
4. `in_image` mode. Use it only with a provider whose `textRendering`
   capability is `reliable`. The placement goes into each panel's `notes`
   so the prompt can state it, and the compiled package lists every string
   under `lettering_text`. After generation, go to step 6 on the render.
5. `overlay` mode. The art is generated with no text. Write
   `lettering.yaml` beside the page file: `page`, `render`, `canvas` (the
   page's `width_px` and `height_px`), `font`, and one entry in `elements`
   per lettering ID with `panel`, `type`, `text` copied from `page.yaml`
   without retyping, `box` in pixels, `shape` (`rect` | `ellipse` |
   `burst` | `cloud` | `none`), `tail`, and `style`. Then run `node
   scripts/letter-pages.js --page <page.yaml> --render <RENDER_ID>`, which
   writes `renders/<RENDER_ID>.lettered.svg` and fails if any text differs
   from the page file.
6. visual-reviewer checks the lettered result on the opened image. Each
   string is compared with `page.yaml` character by character, accents
   included. Each tail points at the planned speaker. The balloons are met
   in their `order`. Nothing the panel is about is hidden. Write the
   outcome, with evidence, into the `lettering` check of the render's
   review file.
7. Route failures by mode. In `overlay` mode, edit `lettering.yaml` and run
   the script again; this costs nothing and the render is untouched. In
   `in_image` mode a failure is a finding in the review, and the fix is
   `/repair-page` with the art locked. If text keeps failing, propose
   overlay mode to the user; the mode is a project setting.
8. Keep overlays tied to their render. When a repair produces a new
   version, update `render` in `lettering.yaml`, check the boxes against
   the new art, and run the script again.
9. Run `node scripts/validate-workspace.js --root production --issue
   <ISS_ID>` and the self-evaluation gates on the lettering files. Report
   per page: mode, elements placed, and the result of the check.

## Outputs

- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/lettering.yaml` (overlay mode),
  validates against `schemas/lettering.schema.json`.
- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/renders/<RENDER_ID>.lettered.svg`
  (overlay mode), written by `letter-pages.js`.
- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/page.yaml`, with placement
  written in the panels' `notes` (`schemas/page.schema.json`).
- The `lettering` check in
  `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/reviews/<RENDER_ID>.review.yaml`
  (`schemas/visual-review.schema.json`).

## Notes

- The text has one home, `page.yaml`. `lettering.yaml` holds geometry and
  a copy that must match. To change a word, change the page file first.
- `letter-pages.js` writes an SVG overlay and does not flatten it into the
  image. Rasterizing for an export that needs flat pages takes a browser
  or a vector tool. The edition records the lettered output in
  `lettered_file`.
- Overlay lettering is free to redo. In-image lettering costs a generation
  per correction, so choose the mode before the first page is rendered.
- Format differences: paged projects keep lettering inside the safe margin
  from `rules/paged/print-specs.md`. Webtoon projects letter for a phone
  screen, with larger type and fewer words per balloon
  (`rules/webtoon/scroll-grammar.md`).
- Reading order follows `rules/lettering/reading-order.md`, and a
  right-to-left project mirrors the placement logic.
- Related: `/panel-script` (owns the words), `/visual-review` (records the
  check), `/repair-page` (in-image corrections), `/build-edition` (ships
  the lettered pages).
